name: Green River Gorge
gaugeName: Green River at Purification Plant near Palmer
blurb: A sheer-walled sandstone gorge an hour from Seattle — spring whitewater controlled by Howard Hanson Dam.

sections.notes: Class II–III whitewater. Headworks is controlled raft and kayak access through the Tacoma Water security gate; check in and follow the guard’s current instructions. No inner-tubing, swimming or general recreation inside the controlled access area. Take out at Kanaskat-Palmer’s upper hand-access site before the harder park rapids. Discover Pass required at the park.

notices.title: Check park gates and river-access signs
notices.text: State Parks lists these day-use areas open for winter 2026–27, with possible temporary weather closures. Hand-launch sites and the actual shore entry may differ from the Area marker. Check current park alerts before setting your shuttle.

notices.title: Controlled raft and kayak launch
notices.text: Tacoma Water identifies a designated boating launch below its diversion. Check in at the guard station before entering; bring identification and vehicle insurance documentation and follow current permit, parking and daylight rules. The watershed is not open for general recreation or inner-tubing.

notices.title: Use the upper Kanaskat take-out
notices.text: Scout the upper hand-access site during your shuttle. The park map warns of Class IV water beyond it; do not continue to the lower access expecting the same difficulty. The Area marker shows the upper day-use vicinity, not the precise exit.

sections.routeReview: Approximate Green River course overview from the designated Headworks access vicinity toward the upper Kanaskat take-out. The line shows general bends and does not identify a landing connection, safe rapid line, navigation route or remaining-time estimate.

putInAccess.note: Tacoma Water’s management plan (printed p. 28) explicitly identifies raft and kayak launching at the upper gravel placement site below the diversion. Its March 2007 access map, hosted by agreement participant American Whitewater, matches the road, buildings and river in current imagery. This is controlled boating access, not general public access to the watershed. The plan excludes unchaperoned swimming, picnicking and inner-tubing. Current gate instructions control; no agency GPS landing fix or verified bank is claimed.
putInAccess.directions: Check in with the Tacoma Water gate guard on SE Green River Headworks Road and obtain permission before entering. Follow the guard’s directions to the designated boating access below the diversion. Bring identification and vehicle insurance documentation; the published access agreement requires these. Launch during daylight and use only the approved access and parking. The Area marker is not an entrance gate or exact landing.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Kanaskat-Palmer State Park
takeOutAccess.note: State Parks explicitly permits hand launching and maps separate upper and lower put-in/take-out sites. The earlier research coordinate matches the upper day-use parking loop and river bend in individual imagery and the agency map. No agency shoreline coordinate is claimed. Class IV water lies downstream of the upper site; the park map says expert boaters only beyond that point. The 2026–27 winter schedule lists day use open, with possible severe-weather closures.
takeOutAccess.directions: Enter Kanaskat-Palmer State Park and follow the day-use road. Use the State Parks map to choose the upper or lower signed hand-launch site for your trip. This Area marker identifies the upper day-use vicinity; it does not pinpoint either shoreline landing. Discover Pass required.

sections.notes: Mercury and Nozzle are Class IV. Remote, steep-walled gorge with few exits — experienced boaters only. Discover Pass required at both Kanaskat-Palmer and Flaming Geyser state parks.

notices.text: The park map distinguishes upper and lower hand-launch sites. Class IV water occurs below the upper site; this gorge trip is for experienced whitewater boaters. The marker shows the upper day-use vicinity, not a precise entry or a rapid-avoidance route.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Flaming Geyser State Park
takeOutAccess.note: The current State Parks page and brochure describe kayaking on the park’s Green River frontage. The candidate matches the eastern picnic-area parking loop, shelters and lodge on the agency brochure and individual imagery, about 100 m inland. Several shoreline entries exist, and none is promoted as an exact landing. The 2026–27 schedule lists day use open but warns of periodic winter closures. This does not assert a developed boat ramp.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed Flaming Geyser State Park entrance and the eastern day-use picnic area near the lodge. Carry boats using an open permitted river-access path and identify your shoreline entry or exit during the shuttle. Discover Pass required; respect gate hours and posted closures.

mapAuditNote: Reviewed 2026-11-09: Tacoma Water confirms controlled raft/kayak access at Headworks. Headworks, Kanaskat-Palmer and Flaming Geyser retain approximate facility-area precision, restrictions and separate section reviews; no exact landing GPS is claimed.
